sourceDirectedNegativeEdges.actualIndividualCoreContrastAndBoundary: Taste/appeal versus younger-sister introductory cores. The shared 未-shaped right side is not semantic identity or an origin analysis. 妹's attested archaicいも/woman/sister meanings are not erased; no universal separation or frequency judgment is made.

Taste/appeal versus speaking/conversation introductory cores. Food can be discussed and 味 has figurative sense/interest uses; a shared situation or figurative domain is not an all-senses separation. Modern 口/未 and 言/舌 shape cues are not histories.

Taste/appeal versus book/origin introductory cores. A book may have appeal and 本 also means base/origin; the source contexts are retained without pretending that short titles exhaust either character's meanings.

Younger-sister versus taste/appeal introductory cores, separately considered in this direction. Shared 未 and the fact that a person can experience taste do not equate the represented relationship and sensation; alternate 妹いも senses remain attested.

Younger-sister versus beginning introductory cores. KanjiPedia始 places 長上の女/originally姒 in なりたち, not its current Japanese meaning list. That history alone is not ordinary 始 meaning sister/woman; neither this distinction nor title differences prove universal negative safety.

Older-sister versus beginning introductory cores. 始's historical 長上の女/姒 account remains visible source evidence, but is not automatically a Japanese lexical attestation or modern frequency proof. Shared シ/女 and a historical account do not clear all senses; actual bounded independent disposition required.

Older-sister versus returning-home introductory cores. A sister can return home, and 帰's bound additional marry/gift meanings must not be erased, but the person/relation and returning action are different represented cores, not universally disjoint semantic inventories.

Beginning versus older-sister introductory cores, separately considered. KanjiPedia's historical 始 account does not by itself establish an ordinary Japanese 始 older-sister sense. Do not silently drop history, infer an unviewed glyph, or claim all-senses ordinary safety.

Beginning versus stand/platform/equipment-counter introductory cores. Modern 台-shaped right side is a mnemonic cue, not permission to equate the whole with 台 or identify an unviewed historical phonetic glyph. Whole accepted 台 also preserves われ/つかさ, without unsupported rarity labels.

Beginning versus younger-sister introductory cores, separately considered. 始's historical elder-woman account and 妹's attested archaic woman/sister uses are not ignored; current beginning and いもうと cores differ, but that is not proof of universal lexical exclusion or quiz necessity.
